profile.name: Roy Wang
profile.headline: AI Product Engineer
profile.tagline: Product-minded engineer building AI-powered tools and interactive web apps.
about: Graduated from National Taiwan Normal University (B.S., Learning Sciences, 2026). My HCI background shapes how I approach the interaction between people and complex systems.
I build AI-powered tools and interactive web apps, across applied NLP, full-stack product interfaces, and interactive UI.
I combine Learning Sciences and engineering practice. I care whether the software is useful to a real person, as well as whether a model can produce an answer.

review.basis: Migrated existing public profile and portfolio; not a new owner attestation.

projects.name: VIRAL - One whisper, a living town
projects.summary: AI-driven town simulation: whisper a sentence to a resident and watch its consequences. Gemma on AMD generates character reactions; a deterministic engine validates actions and records causal events.
projects.contribution: Public project in RoyWG925's account. Individual versus team ownership of specific components remains unconfirmed.
results: Published a playable experience with validated model actions and an inspectable chain of causes.
limitations: Live runs depend on model latency. Entertainment claims have not been validated with human playtesters.
Submission, acceptance, awards, and Roy's precise team contribution are not confirmed.
lessons: Separate model-generated decisions from deterministic state changes and make failures observable.

review.basis: Public repository describes the project; does not attest to individual contribution or competition outcome.

projects.name: Market Sentiment x TAIEX
projects.summary: Three-person NTNU event study of PTT Stock sentiment and the TAIEX. Fine-tuned multilingual BERT and evaluated sentiment structure around the April 2025 tariff shock.
projects.contribution: Roy handled BERT training, coding, crawling, and statistical analysis in a three-person NTNU research team, as described in the existing public portfolio.
results: Implemented a text ingestion, labeling, model training, and event-study workflow.
limitations: The reported 0.683 macro-F1 used a test set overlapping training and tuning. The repository reports 0.580 on a 45-item consensus-labeled holdout.
This is a single-event, same-day association study; it does not establish market prediction.
lessons: Separate exploratory scores from held-out evaluation and publish corrections when recomputation changes the conclusion.

review.basis: Current public README and corrections supersede historical resume claims.

projects.name: Is my major worth it?
projects.summary: Interactive dashboard comparing Taiwan university admission scores with graduate salaries across 1,787 programs, with field-level salary distributions and methodology notes.
projects.contribution: NTNU course project authored by Roy Wang, as credited in the public README.
results: Joined admission and field-level salary data and built an interactive exploration interface.
limitations: Salary data are at field level, not individual program outcomes. No public server demo is documented.
lessons: Make data grain and proxy assumptions visible alongside comparisons.

review.basis: Migrated current public README and existing profile.
